text: Hi! I'm PIP! Welcome aboard Mailwing!
We’re part of Cosmic Mail. We carry important stories across the stars!
Every explorer has a file in the Cosmic Archive. See how their records connect?
Wait... one of the records just lost its connection.
Another one... and now the third!
Huh? That’s strange...
The archive is trying to reconnect them, but the pieces don’t match.
Wait... these records aren’t connecting anymore!
I know these explorers... but some of my own records are missing.
I can’t remember everything they discovered.
But wait! I still have some old locations!
Maybe we can find them and put their stories back together!
Three incomplete files. Three silent signals.
Will you help me bring their stories back?
Then let's make it official! Every Cosmic Mail Carrier needs a name.
Your passport is ready. Let me show you around the cabin.
This is your Cosmic Passport. It keeps every history we bring back to Earth.
The navigation screen shows approximate signals. Mars is the closest one.
Pick the signal, confirm the route, then press the red button.
When you find the explorer, use the scanner. I'll help you recognize its parts.
Welcome back, carrier. The archive is waiting for your next delivery.
Route ready! Press the red button when you're set!
Here we go. Let's bring this memory home.
We're here! The signal is somewhere ahead. Let's take a look!
Look! Something's over there. Could that be our missing explorer?
It looks like an old rover, resting in the dust. Its tools might tell us what it studied.
My archive just reconnected a record. This is Spirit, a Mars Exploration Rover! It was sent to study rocks and soil for clues about ancient water.
Press Q to take out your Cosmic Scanner.
Tap the scanner button to take out your Cosmic Scanner.
Aim at one of the rover's tools and hold the scan button. I'll explain what we find.
Something on the explorer is responding. Hold the scan to recognize this part.
Keep holding... the scanner is reading this part.
The reading stopped. Hold the scan button a little longer when you're ready.
These are Spirit's panoramic cameras! They helped scientists see the landscape and choose where to explore.
This tool brushed and ground away the rock's outer surface. Scientists could then study the material underneath!
This instrument studied infrared light to help scientists learn what Martian materials were made of!
Look at the cameras near the top of Spirit!
There's an interesting tool near its robotic arm!
One more instrument is waiting beside the cameras!
The Pancam is still missing. Aim at the cameras at the top of the mast and hold the scan button.
The RAT is still missing. Aim at the tool on the robotic arm and hold the scan button.
Mini-TES is still missing. Aim at the instrument beside the cameras and hold the scan button.
We've found all the clues! Let's scan the whole explorer!
The archive needs a full recognition scan of the complete explorer before its memory can be recovered.
All three parts are recognized. The Cosmic Archive can now study the complete explorer.
Hold still... I'm linking the three fragments into one record.
OBJETO COMPLETO — MEMORIA RECUPERADA.
The memory is safe! Now we can create a smart letter and bring this story back to Earth.
The smart letter is ready. It carries Spirit's identity, journey, discoveries and the end of its mission.
We did it! Now we can bring this explorer's story back to Earth. Return to Mailwing and transmit the letter.
Our job is to recognize this explorer's parts, recover its memory and send its story to Earth. The Cosmic Radar points toward the signal.
The tools that helped it study the landscape are usually on the mast and the robotic arm. Aim there and hold the scan.
Use your Cosmic Scanner on the explorer's tools. Look closely at the mast and the robotic arm.
We still have fragments missing. The explorer is waiting for another scan.
The smart letter is ready in the cabin archive. Return to Mailwing to transmit it.
This history is restored. The archive on Earth has its copy.
Every part is recognized. Open the full recognition scan when you are ready; it studies the complete explorer, not a single part.
The memory is recovered. Prepare the smart letter and carry it back to Mailwing to transmit it to Earth.
This history is restored. You can review it in the passport at any time.
The wind here is very thin. Every dust grain has been waiting a long time.
Those rocks look ancient. I wonder what stories they could tell us.
We did it! Spirit may be silent now, but what it discovered will never be forgotten.
The Cosmic Scanner can read the landscape too. Press Q and try it on a rock or a patch of soil.
The Cosmic Scanner can read the landscape too. Tap the scanner button and try it on a rock or a patch of soil.
The Cosmic Scanner can read the landscape too. Aim at a rock, a soil patch or a formation and hold the scan.
This dark rock looks volcanic. I am comparing its shape and tone with Martian basalt references.
Volcanic rocks like this can preserve the story of ancient lava. The scanner sees a match in texture, but only a laboratory can confirm the minerals.
This looks like fine Martian dust over broken rock. The surface is loose and easy for the wind to move.
The scanner sees a mix of dust and grains. Regolith covers much of Mars, and its patterns can hide the rock underneath.
These streaks look shaped by the wind. The scanner is reading the ripple pattern, not the weather.
Wind moves sand and dust into ripples and long streaks. The scanner compares the pattern with reference dunes. It is an observation, not a measurement of today's wind.
This layered outcrop may record ancient changes. The scanner sees stacked layers worth a closer look.
Layered rocks can preserve evidence of past water or changing environments. The scanner compares the visible layers with reference geology; the full story needs more data.
Let's keep our boots on the ground for now. I need a clear ground survey before we fly over the site.
